title: WORKSHEET 14
subject: Past Perfect Tense & Past Perfect Continuous
subjectVi: Ngữ pháp bài 14: Past Perfect Tense & Past Perfect Continuous

sections.instruction: Supply a suitable SIMPLE PAST or PAST PERFECT TENSE:

questions.prompt: They [gap] (go) home after they [gap] (finish) their work.
acceptedAnswers: went / had finished

questions.prompt: She [gap] (just / go) out when I called her.
acceptedAnswers: had just gone
questions.explanation: finished just before a past moment → past perfect

questions.prompt: My brother [gap] (eat) all the pie before we got back.
acceptedAnswers: had eaten

questions.prompt: He wondered why I [gap] (not / visit) him before.
acceptedAnswers: hadn't visited

questions.prompt: She said that she [gap] (already / see) the Pyramids.
acceptedAnswers: had already seen

questions.prompt: The fire [gap] (spread) to the next building before the firemen [gap] (arrive).
acceptedAnswers: had spread / arrived
questions.explanation: earlier action → past perfect; before + simple past

questions.prompt: They drank small cups of coffee, after they [gap] (finish) dinner.
acceptedAnswers: had finished

questions.prompt: He told me he [gap] (catch) a young lion.
acceptedAnswers: had caught

questions.prompt: His mother [gap] (worry) a lot about him before she [gap] (hear) that he was safe.
acceptedAnswers: had worried|worried / heard
questions.explanation: earlier action → past perfect; before + simple past

questions.prompt: He [gap] (already / learn) English before he [gap] (leave) for England, but before he arrived in England, he [gap] (forget) some.
acceptedAnswers: had already learned|had already learnt / left / had forgotten
questions.explanation: actions before a past moment → past perfect

questions.prompt: Mary [gap] (go) swimming after she [gap] (come) home. After she [gap] (swim), she [gap] (call) her friend Judy.
acceptedAnswers: went / had come / had swum / called
questions.explanation: after + past perfect; then simple past

questions.prompt: I [gap] (go) to the theatre with my friends yesterday. I [gap] (not / go) to the theatre for a year. We [gap] (have) a very good time.
acceptedAnswers: went / hadn't been|hadn't gone / had
questions.explanation: period up to a past moment → past perfect

questions.prompt: After they [gap] (finish) their breakfast, they [gap] (leave) for school.
acceptedAnswers: had finished / left
questions.explanation: after + past perfect; then simple past

questions.prompt: Linda [gap] (play) tennis after she [gap] (do) her homework.
acceptedAnswers: played / had done

questions.prompt: My father [gap] (water) the flowers after he [gap] (clean) the car. After he [gap] (water) the flowers, he [gap] (have) dinner.
acceptedAnswers: watered / had cleaned / had watered / had
questions.explanation: after + past perfect; then simple past

sections.instruction: Combine the following sentences by using AFTER / BEFORE (use the PAST PERFECT for the earlier action):

questions.prompt: My mother took her umbrella. She went out.
acceptedAnswers: After my mother had taken her umbrella, she went out.
My mother went out after she had taken her umbrella.
My mother had taken her umbrella before she went out.
Before she went out, my mother had taken her umbrella.
My mother took her umbrella before she went out.
questions.explanation: earlier action → past perfect; after/before links the two

sections.instruction: Read the passage and answer the questions:
sections.contextText:
I had an amusing experience last year. After I had left a small village in the south of France, I drove on to the next town. On the way a young man waved to me. I stopped and he asked me for a lift. After he had got into the car, I said good morning to him in French and he replied in the same language.
Except a few words, I do not know any French at all. Neither of us spoke during the journey.
I had nearly reached the town, when the young man suddenly said, very slowly, “Do you speak English?”
As I soon learned, he was English himself!

questions.prompt: When did the writer drive on to the next town?
acceptedAnswers: After he had left a small village in the south of France.
He drove on to the next town after he had left a small village in the south of France.
After he had left a small village in the south of France, he drove on to the next town.
After the writer had left a small village in the south of France.

questions.prompt: When did he say good morning to the man in French?
acceptedAnswers: After the young man had got into the car.
After he had got into the car.
He said good morning to him in French after the young man had got into the car.
He said good morning to the man in French after he had got into the car.

questions.prompt: When did the young man say, “Do you speak English?”
acceptedAnswers: When the writer had nearly reached the town.
When he had nearly reached the town.
He said it when the writer had nearly reached the town.
When they had nearly reached the town.

questions.prompt: He [gap] (live) in London for ten years when he had an accident.

questions.prompt: He was tired because he [gap] (write) letters all morning.

sections.instruction: Fill in the following sentences by using the PAST PERFECT CONTINUOUS TENSE:
